isolation: the greeter is a stateless read-only GET endpoint with no shared mutable state; each scenario is an independent request asserted on its own response

scenarios.rule: A caller who supplies a name receives a greeting that includes it

steps.text: the response is a JSON greeting that includes "Ada"
steps.observed: response is valid JSON with content-type application/json; both "name":"Ada" and message "Hello, Ada!" include "Ada"

scenarios.rule: A caller who omits the name still receives a valid default greeting

steps.text: an API Consumer calls "GET /hello" with no name parameter
the response is a JSON greeting with a default name
steps.command: curl -s --max-time 10 "$BASE/hello" | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); assert d['name'] and d['message']"
steps.observed: name field is non-empty default "World"; message is "Hello, World!"

scenarios.rule: A caller who omits the name still receives a valid default greeting
scenarios.scenario: Greeting with an empty name supplied

steps.text: the response is a JSON greeting with a default name
steps.command: curl -s --max-time 10 "$BASE/hello?name=" | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); assert d['name'] and d['message']"
steps.observed: empty name query param falls back to the same default name "World"; message is "Hello, World!"
